steps.description: Acquire 20 coal for the starter iron cell.

execution_guidance.approach: Gather 20 coal from a natural coal resource for both starter machines.
execution_guidance.rationale: At the observed rates, 50 iron needs about 7.5 coal for drilling and 3.6 for smelting. Twenty provides startup margin without a large fuel expedition.
constraints: No machine crafting is needed for this slice.
Fuel quantities are finite bootstrap stock, not automated delivery.

steps.description: Install the held burner-mining-drill on iron ore; obtain its fresh identity and actual output geometry before furnace placement.

execution_guidance.approach: Use the held drill with a live resource-covering placement candidate; read its fresh output geometry before proceeding.
execution_guidance.rationale: Direct feeding reuses owned equipment, avoids about 100 seconds of hand mining for 50 ore, and permits overlapping work. Its 15 ore/min rate is slower than manual mining but needs no new machine investment.
constraints: Use the one held burner-mining-drill.
Validate actual iron coverage and a usable output location.
End at the new-identity and output-geometry boundary.

steps.description: Install the held stone-furnace at a freshly validated candidate covering the drill output; obtain its fresh identity before fueling.

execution_guidance.approach: Use the held furnace at a candidate whose footprint covers the freshly observed drill output; then read its identity and the actual route.
execution_guidance.rationale: The owned stone furnace can smelt 18.75 plates/min, exceeding the drill's 15 ore/min. One pair suffices for this bootstrap; extra cells add setup cost before any cell is proven.
constraints: Use the one held stone-furnace.
Presence alone does not prove direct output connectivity.
Verify the route before supplying fuel.

steps.description: Fuel the direct-fed iron cell, smelt 50 new iron plates, and collect at least 58 iron plates in total; verify steam-power is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Supply coal to both exact machines, verify direct-fed smelting, and collect output until 58 iron plates are held and steam-power is researched.
execution_guidance.rationale: Eight iron plates are already held and no preceding step consumes them. Fifty new plates satisfy the exact production trigger; drilling takes about 200 seconds, excluding setup and final smelting.
constraints: Do not hand-supply iron ore; use the selected direct-feed method.
Verify steam-power after its native production trigger.
Defer autonomous fuel delivery and further construction to later slices.

steps.description: Acquire 10 copper ore for the electronics bootstrap.

execution_guidance.approach: Gather 10 copper ore from natural resources by hand.
execution_guidance.rationale: Live mining facts give 20 seconds of hand mining versus 40 seconds with one burner drill for 10 ore, excluding travel and setup. Another cell adds crafting, placement and fuel costs for this small batch.
constraints: Acquire exactly the missing 10 copper ore.
This is finite bootstrap stock, not autonomous copper production.
Do not dismantle buildings to acquire materials.

steps.description: Use the existing furnace to smelt and collect 10 copper plates; verify electronics is researched while preserving both iron-cell structures and their direct-output route.

execution_guidance.approach: Re-observe the furnace at (-72,2), remove residual iron output, supply 10 copper ore, collect 10 copper plates, and verify electronics.
execution_guidance.rationale: The observed furnace has 5 coal. Ten plates need about 0.72 coal and 32 seconds of smelting. Reuse avoids another furnace’s 5-stone cost and placement; a dedicated copper cell can pay back during later sustained production.
constraints: Read fresh furnace inventories and bind its exact identity before transfers.
Preserve units 29 and 30 and their native direct-output route.
Verify electronics after its production trigger; do not submit it as lab research.

steps.description: Acquire 5 copper ore for the lab’s remaining copper requirement.

execution_guidance.approach: Gather the missing 5 copper ore from natural resources by hand.
execution_guidance.rationale: Live rates give 10 seconds of hand mining versus 20 seconds of burner-drill production, excluding travel and setup. A dedicated cell is unnecessary for this finite shortfall.
constraints: Acquire only the missing 5 copper ore.
This bootstrap does not establish autonomous copper supply.
Do not dismantle buildings for materials.

steps.description: Smelt the 5 copper ore and collect enough plates to hold 15 copper plates, preserving the existing iron-cell structures and their direct-output route.

execution_guidance.approach: Re-observe the furnace at (-72,2), supply 5 copper ore, then collect 5 additional copper plates.
execution_guidance.rationale: The furnace was observed with 4 coal and empty output. Five plates require about 16 seconds of smelting; reuse avoids another furnace and its placement cost.
constraints: Read fresh inventories before exact transfers.
Preserve units 29 and 30 and the drill-to-furnace direct-output route.
Verify 15 copper plates held before downstream crafting.

steps.description: Craft one lab using 10 electronic circuits, 10 iron gear wheels and 4 transport belts; verify automation-science-pack technology is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Resolve live component recipes, craft the lab’s 10 circuits, 10 gears and 4 belts, then craft one lab and verify the technology trigger.
execution_guidance.rationale: Ten circuits require 30 cable, made by 15 cable crafts using 15 copper plates. Reuse the 74 held iron plates; validate the combined remaining component bill before crafting.
constraints: Resolve exact missing dependencies using fresh recipe and inventory facts.
Keep the lab in inventory for the later powered-research slice.
Verify the craft-item lab trigger; do not submit this technology as lab research.

steps.description: Prepare one offshore pump and one boiler from 11 iron plates and 5 newly collected stone, preserving the existing iron-cell structures and their direct-output route.

execution_guidance.approach: Harvest 5 stone, craft a new furnace, 2 gears and 7 pipes, then craft one offshore pump and one boiler. Verify both finished items in inventory.
execution_guidance.rationale: Enabled recipes require 11 iron plates and 5 stone together; 38 iron plates are held. A new furnace avoids dismantling the iron cell. Defer further construction until shoreline geometry is observed.
constraints: Preserve units 29 and 30 and the drill-to-furnace direct-output route.
Craft a new furnace for the boiler; do not consume the placed furnace.
Next construction boundary needs fresh water, pump candidates and placed pump geometry.

steps.description: Install one offshore pump at the observed shoreline near (47.5, 1.5), using the held pump and preserving the existing iron-cell structures and direct-output route.

execution_guidance.approach: Approach the observed shoreline, refresh native water and pump candidates, then install the held pump with place_candidate. Stop at the placed-identity boundary.
execution_guidance.rationale: A legal pump candidate was observed at (47.5, 1.5), direction 8. Reusing the held pump avoids additional crafting; boiler placement requires the installed pump’s live outlet geometry.
constraints: Preserve units 29 and 30 and their direct drill-to-furnace route.
Refresh water and placement candidates after arrival; use place_candidate.
Read the installed pump’s identity and outlet before planning boiler connections.

steps.description: Install one held burner-mining-drill covering copper ore; observe its fresh identity and actual output position.

execution_guidance.approach: Reuse the held burner drill for direct copper-ore feeding; validate resource-covering placement and then read its runtime output geometry.
execution_guidance.rationale: Both machines are already held, so this method adds no machine-crafting cost. Manual mining may finish ten ore sooner, but direct feed removes ore hand-supply and establishes a reusable cell.
constraints: Use a live candidate covering copper ore.
Stop at placement to obtain fresh identity and output geometry.
Do not add duplicate production cells.

steps.description: Install one held stone-furnace covering the drill’s observed output; verify the direct ore route using fresh identities.

execution_guidance.approach: Reuse the held furnace and select a placement covering the newly observed drill output; inspect the resulting native item route.
execution_guidance.rationale: A separate observation boundary avoids guessing the drill's rotated output. Direct ore delivery reduces repeated transfers; furnace fuel remains a separate requirement.
constraints: Check the live copper-smelting recipe and furnace compatibility.
Use the drill output as covers_position, not as a guessed center.
Obtain the placed furnace identity before exact supply.

steps.description: Fuel the cell, produce and collect 10 copper plates, and verify that electronics is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Fuel both exact machines from the coal stock, allow direct-fed smelting, collect ten plates and verify the electronics trigger.
execution_guidance.rationale: Only ten copper plates are required for this milestone. Additional cells are not justified before the first cell is proven; this bootstrap does not claim sustained automated fuel supply.
constraints: Observe both exact identities before supplying fuel.
Use live recipe rates for production waiting and fuel allocation.
Verify electronics rather than submitting it as lab research.

steps.description: Prepare one stone-furnace, 50 iron ore and at least 4 coal for the steam-power bootstrap.

execution_guidance.approach: Acquire 5 stone and craft one stone-furnace; hand-mine 50 iron ore. Keep at least 4 coal from the 10 held.
execution_guidance.rationale: Hand mining takes 100 seconds for 50 ore versus 200 seconds for one burner drill, before setup. An additional drill also exceeds the 8 held plates in total iron cost; finite manual bootstrap avoids that dependency.
constraints: Gather only missing kit quantities.
Retain the 8 held iron plates.
Do not repurpose existing copper machinery.

steps.description: Install the new stone-furnace within 16 tiles of (-75, -36), retaining the existing copper cell; observe the new furnace’s identity.

execution_guidance.approach: Place the new furnace on clear ground within radius 16 of (-75,-36), then observe its exact identity before supplying it.
execution_guidance.rationale: A separate furnace avoids switching the copper route. End at placement because the next exact transfer needs the new live identity; the count checkpoint proves presence only.
constraints: Preserve drill 27, furnace 28 and their direct item route.
Use one new furnace, not another drill.
Observe the new identity before exact supply.

steps.description: Smelt 50 new iron plates in the new furnace, collect them to hold at least 58 iron plates, and verify steam-power is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Supply the new exact furnace with 50 iron ore and 4 coal, verify smelting, collect 50 plates, and verify the steam-power trigger.
execution_guidance.rationale: One furnace needs 160 seconds of smelting and 3.6 coal for 50 plates. Four coal covers this finite batch. Native new plate production, not held starting plates, fulfills the research trigger.
constraints: Do not feed iron ore into copper furnace 28.
Use live output checkpoints rather than guessed wait ticks.
Verify steam-power researched; it is not lab research.

steps.description: Collect five copper plates from the existing copper furnace, holding at least 15 copper plates and 36 iron plates for one lab.

execution_guidance.approach: Collect five copper plates from exact furnace 28 at (-75,-36), retaining at least 36 iron plates.
execution_guidance.rationale: Nine copper plates are already in the furnace and ten are held. Collecting the deficit avoids mining, smelting time and extra machine setup.
constraints: Preserve machines 27, 28 and 29 and the existing direct copper-ore route.
Use the observed exact furnace identity for transfer.
Verify inventory after collection.

steps.description: Craft one lab from the prepared materials and verify automation-science-pack is researched.

execution_guidance.approach: Resolve live crafting dependencies for one lab: 12 gears, 30 cables, 10 circuits and four belts; craft the lab and verify its research trigger.
execution_guidance.rationale: The combined bill is 36 iron plates and 15 copper plates. Hand crafting needs no powered machinery, and the lab remains available for later research.
constraints: Use 15 cable crafts and two belt crafts for their required output quantities.
Resolve missing dependencies before downstream crafts and verify crafting results.
Keep the lab in inventory and verify automation-science-pack researched.

steps.description: Prepare one offshore pump, one boiler, one steam engine, two small electric poles and ten spare pipes, preserving the existing copper drill and both furnaces.

execution_guidance.approach: Inspect exact furnaces 28 and 29, collect available plates, acquire only missing materials, and craft the five-item kit. Stop with the hardware held for fresh shoreline and connection observations.
execution_guidance.rationale: The combined bill is 52 iron plates, one copper plate, five stone and one wood; 22 iron plates are held. Stored outputs avoid mining and setup. Reuse the copper cell if necessary; another cell or furnace row is unnecessary for this kit.
constraints: Preserve units 27, 28 and 29 and drill 27's direct output route into furnace 28.
Crafting requires 10 gears, 22 pipes, one furnace and two cables; one pole craft yields two.
Verify all held kit quantities; installation and functional power verification belong to later work.

steps.description: Install one offshore pump within 12 tiles of (51, 8), preserving the existing copper drill and both furnaces.

execution_guidance.approach: Approach the shoreline, refresh water and legal pump candidates, and install the held pump using place_candidate. Stop before boiler placement.
execution_guidance.rationale: The pump is held and native shoreline candidates exist about 129 tiles away. No crafting is needed. The next connection requires the installed pump’s identity and actual outlet geometry.
constraints: Preserve units 27, 28 and 29 and drill 27’s direct output into furnace 28.
Refresh water and pump candidates after arrival; install only through place_candidate.
Verify pump presence, then observe its exact identity and outlet before boiler planning.
